claims.statement: crates/ holds five in-repo format crates — gdi-rs (port of gdidrop, BSD-2-Clause, CLI gdirs), nsz-rs (nsz, MIT, nszrs), xdelta-rs (xdelta3, Apache-2.0, xdeltars), xps-rs (Flips, GPL-3.0-or-later, xpsrs) and xso-rs (maxcso, ISC, xsors) — that replaced the external tools oxyromon used to shell out to. They are workspace members via `members = ["crates/*"]`, sharing the root lockfile and CI, while frontend/ and desktop/ declare their own workspaces and stay out of the native build.

Every crate entry point is synchronous and file-to-file: input path, output path, a settings struct, and `progress: &mut dyn FnMut(u64)` called with input bytes consumed since the last call, the calls summing to an input size the caller can compute up front — the ISO/BIN/container for xso, gdi and nsz, the patch for xdelta and xps. gdi-rs additionally exports `input_size(cue)` because that total spans several BINs, and counts a dropped pregap as consumed.

oxyromon adapts the crate contract in one place, `progress::run_blocking(progress_bar, length, work)`: it clones the shared bar, moves the closure to tokio's blocking pool, resets the bar to the bytes style with `length`, and feeds `bar.inc` to the crate's callback, mapping a JoinError to "Conversion task failed" separately from the crate's own error. Callers pass `input.metadata()?.len()`, or `gdi_rs::input_size(&cue)` for a CUE whose BINs are the real input.

All five crates write to `<output>.part` beside the destination and rename it into place only on success, removing it on any failure; the same `part`/`finish` pair is duplicated per crate (xso-rs shares it through `crate::io`). The guarantees — an existing output is replaced only by a complete file, and a failed run leaves nothing behind — are tested per crate, and nsz-rs's `with_output` additionally creates the parent directory and drops the File before renaming, which Windows requires.

gdi-rs commits atomically across a whole file set: `plan` validates the CUE layout, the existing output directory and the rule that no track may be written over a BIN the CUE reads before anything is created, then every track and the `.gdi` descriptor are written as `.part` files and renamed only after the last succeeds, with all of them removed on failure. A rejected input therefore leaves a pre-existing set untouched.

Each crate exposes one thiserror `Error` plus a `Result<T>` alias, with identical wording for the shared variants: `Io` ("io error: …", `#[from] std::io::Error`) and `Corrupt` in all five; `BadMagic { expected, found }` and `Unsupported` in xso-rs, nsz-rs, xdelta-rs and xps-rs; `InvalidOption` in xso-rs, gdi-rs and xdelta-rs. Crates add only format-specific variants (nsz-rs: MissingKey, InvalidKey, Verification, Compression, Hex).

`WrongSource` exists only in the two patch crates and means the patch is well formed but this is not its file: BPS raises it after verifying the patch's own CRC and then the source's size and CRC (with a distinct message when the "source" is already the patch's output), and xdelta-rs raises it when a rebuilt window fails its Adler-32 check.

xps-rs reports Flips' three suspicions about an IPS patch (NotThis, AlreadyApplied, Scrambled) as `Option<Warning>` from `apply` while still applying it, because IPS carries no checksum; oxyromon prints it as "Patched, but …". BPS instead refuses a wrong source outright.

Each CLI is a clap-builder `cli()` plus one `convert` closure around a shared `src/bin/<cli>/ui.rs` that is byte-identical in all five crates, and `tests/crates.rs` asserts the copies in gdirs, nszrs, xdeltars and xpsrs equal xsors's — so the shared shell can only be changed in all five at once.

The shared shell fixes the user-visible contract for every tool: `<cli> [OPTIONS] <INPUT>...` with each input converted in the direction its extension implies, `-o DIR` defaulting to next to each input and created on demand, oxyROMon's progress-bar template, one ✔/✖ result line per input, and a non-zero exit if any input failed. `Outputs::claim` compares absolute paths so no output lands on an input or on an earlier input's output.

The patch CLIs add their own guards around the shared shell: neither xpsrs nor xdeltars may write an output that resolves to the `-s` source, xpsrs names each output after the patch with the source's extension, and xdeltars prefers the target name a patch records — reduced to a bare file name so a recorded path cannot escape the output directory.

Manifests are library-first: `[features] default = ["cli"]` with `cli = ["dep:clap", "dep:console", "dep:indicatif"]`, the `[[bin]]` gated on `required-features = ["cli"]`, and oxyromon depending on each crate by `path` and `version` with `default-features = false` so it links none of the CLI UI stack. `edition`, `rust-version`, `repository` and shared dependencies come from `[workspace.package]`/`[workspace.dependencies]`, and no crate declares `[profile]` since only the root's applies.

Releases are per crate: its own version, its own CHANGELOG.md in oxyromon's format, and git tags named `<crate>-<version>`. A crate must be published before an oxyromon release that needs its new version, because the root pins each dependency by path and version. `dist.sh` cross-compiles and packages the five CLIs alongside oxyromon for every target.

nsz-rs takes keys as a loader (`impl FnOnce() -> Result<Keys>`) invoked only when the pipeline needs one — compression reaches it at the first `.nca` member, decompression only when verifying against a CNMT — so unverified decompression and containers with no NCAs (homebrew) never need `prod.keys`. Keys load from `~/.switch/prod.keys` (`-k` for the CLI) and are CRC32-verified against known source/master-key checksums, matching the Python tool's sanity check; `--skip-key-check` covers synthetic keys, and key-read errors name the file because the failure surfaces far from the path.

oxyromon's `nsz::get_version()` never fails but returns "built-in, prod.keys not found" when `~/.switch/prod.keys` is absent — a warning rather than an error precisely because only compressing NSPs containing NCAs needs keys; its decompression path runs `decompress_nsz` with `fix_padding = true, verify = false, strict = false`.

Malformed inputs must fail as errors, never panic or allocate on untrusted header fields: crafted `NCZSECTN` section counts (1<<40, i64::MAX, -1) and PFS0 fields (u32::MAX file count, u64::MAX member offset) are rejected; xso-rs bounds a block's stored span so a corrupt index cannot request gigabytes; nsz-rs refuses an implausible Meta NCA size before decompressing it.

Crate tests check agreement with the reference implementation rather than self-consistency — xso-rs against maxcso ($MAXCSO/$PATH, including byte-identical output vs `maxcso --only-zlib`), xdelta-rs against `xdelta3`, xps-rs against `flips`, nsz-rs against vectors from `scripts/gen_vectors.py` — and they skip rather than fail when the tool is missing; CI installs xdelta3 specifically so the xdelta-rs comparison runs.
